result.rationale: Verified mechanism: in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not produce a zod catchall — ZodType does not override toString, so both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]". The resulting schema is `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })` (duplicate key, last wins), which strips all other fields. In sync mode (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set), parseRefreshTokenResponse uses this schema, so expiry fields like expiry_date/expire

The resulting schema is `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })` (duplicate key, last wins), which strips all other fields. In sync mode (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set), parseRefreshTokenResponse uses this schema, so expiry fields like expiry_date/expires_in are stripped before the credential is persisted (e.g. office365 CalendarService spreads tokenResponse.data into o365AuthCredentials, and the Google path also routes through parseRefreshTokenResponse in sync mode). Result: stale/missing expiry persisted, causing repeated refreshes against the external sync endpoint or 401s. This is a real, verifiable defect in newly added code.

judged_text: The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to fixed literal strings (Object.prototype.toString, i.e. '[object Object]'), not a catchall, so minimumTokenResponseSchema is a fixed-shape object that keeps only access_token and strips every other field — the expiry the adjacent comments promise is never captured. In sync mode every refreshed token is persisted without a fresh expiry (spread-based call sites like office365 and zoom retain the stale old expiryDate), so expiry-gated refresh fires on every calendar operation, hammering CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with one external call plus a credential write per request, or the expiry is undefined and 401s surface instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate at definition time to a single literal key (the ZodString object's `toString()` result, typically `"[object Object]"`), not a “catchall”. Zod `z.object()` also strips unknown keys by default, so this schema cannot capture arbitrary numeric expiry fields as the comments intend and will likely fail parsing unless the response literally contains that key. This directly breaks sync-mode token parsing (and can lead to missing/incorrect expiry handling in callers relying on the parsed data).
